report.summary: Two causes account for all four failures, and each test appears in exactly one. First, fix the product bug: `list_books` in app/main.py never filters by owner, so every user sees every user's books. That breaks the API isolation test and the new-user empty-state UI test. Second, fix the test bug: the page object clicks `add-books` while the template's button is `add-book`, which breaks both UI add-book tests. The page-object fix is a one-line change and can go in immediately.

causes.title: GET /api/books and the /books page list every user's books
causes.explanation: list_books(user_id) ignores user_id and runs an unfiltered SELECT over the books table. Any logged-in user therefore sees all books, including other users' private books. get_own_book does filter by owner_id, so single-book GET and DELETE correctly return 404 for other users' books. Only the list endpoint and the server-rendered table leak data. This is a real data-isolation bug, and it is deterministic, so it is not flaky. The API test fails on the list check before it reaches its 404 assertions. The UI test sees rows created by other tests in the same session, so the new user's bookshelf is not empty.
evidence: app/main.py:147-150: def list_books(user_id: int) -> list[dict]: ... rows = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM books ORDER BY id").fetchall()  (user_id is never used)
app/main.py:163-170: get_own_book filters with "WHERE id = ? AND owner_id = ?" (so the single-book endpoints are correct)
tests\api\test_books_api.py:42: assert 2 not in [1, 2]  (other user's list contains the first user's book id 2)
tests\ui\test_login_ui.py:14: AssertionError: Locator expected to be visible / Actual value: None / Error: element(s) not found for get_by_test_id("empty-state")
Aria snapshot of the new user's /books page lists rows "Final title Someone 2001 Delete" and "From API-7eba9a2e Robot Delete", which belong to other users and tests
causes.suggested_fix: Filter the query by owner: "SELECT * FROM books WHERE owner_id = ? ORDER BY id" with (user_id,) in list_books. Add a regression test that asserts the list endpoint and the /books page show only the caller's books.

causes.title: Page object uses the wrong test id for the Add book button
causes.explanation: BooksPage.add clicks get_by_test_id("add-books"), but the template's submit button is data-testid="add-book". The locator matches nothing, so the click waits for the full 5 s timeout and fails before any app behaviour is exercised. The app is correct here. The page object is the outlier: the same file's delete locator ("delete-book") matches the template, and test_deleted_book_disappears uses it without problems. This is deterministic, not flaky.
evidence: tests\ui\test_books_ui.py failure: playwright._impl._errors.TimeoutError: Locator.click: Timeout 5000ms exceeded. Call log: - waiting for get_by_test_id("add-books")
Both failing UI tests report the same call log, and the test_future_year test fails at books.add(...) before reaching its assertions
causes.suggested_fix: Change tests/support/pages.py:44 to get_by_test_id("add-book"). Confidence is high, but I could not check git history to confirm which side changed most recently, so confirm against the template in version control before merging.
